title: Battery life of a mesh node
question: How long will a node run on batteries, and what actually drains them?

headlines.detail: 17.6 mW average, routing for its neighbours

headlines.label: of the energy is spent listening

summary: Every node in a wayfinder mesh is a router, so its receiver never sleeps: it has to hear its neighbours' routing adverts to keep its routes. An open LoRa receiver draws about 17 mW whether or not anything arrives, and that dominates everything else. A typical sensor here spends 94% of its energy listening and lasts 21 days on 2x AA lithium. Its transmissions (its readings, plus relayed adverts) barely register, which is why slowing the advert schedule hardly changes battery life (chart 2). The lever that matters is a receiver that can sleep between frames. Chart 4 prices the same measured traffic at lower listening power to show what that would be worth. A sensor that didn't route at all would last 10 years, which is the cost of being part of a mesh.

charts.title: Where the energy goes (per hour)
charts.caption: Listening, with the receiver open waiting for frames, outweighs everything the radio actually sends or receives.

charts.title: Battery life vs. advert interval
charts.caption: Nearly flat: fewer adverts save transmit and receive energy, but listening costs the same.

What a sleeping receiver would be worth (upper bound)
charts.caption: 17 mW is an always-open receiver, today's behaviour. Lower values re-price the same measured traffic.

method: The network and channel are the crowded-LoRa scenario's: SF7 at 868 MHz, 1% duty cycle, 6 sensors plus a gateway, one reading per 120 s. Every radio's transmit, receive and idle time is metered from the simulated medium over one hour after warm-up and priced for an SX1262-class radio at 3.3 V (150 mW transmit, 17 mW receive or listening). Batteries: 2x AA lithium ≈ 9 Wh. The listening-power and sleeping-leaf figures re-price measured activity and are upper bounds: wayfinder does not doze its receiver today, and a dozing receiver would miss frames this model does not account for.
